My journey

My Biography – The Journey of Mr. Rahman

An honest story of learning, persistence and a hope to make a positive difference.

From a rural background to a bigger vision

My name is Saidur Rahman, and I am publicly known as Mr. Rahman. I come from a rural background in Sribhumi district, Assam, India. My journey has taught me that circumstances may create challenges, but they do not have to decide the limits of our dreams.

Like many students from rural areas, reaching school and continuing my education was not always easy. Long walks to school and the challenges of my surroundings became part of my learning journey. Those experiences strengthened my belief in education, patience and consistent effort.

I completed my Class 12 education in the Science stream and am currently pursuing graduation. Alongside my studies, I work as an educator and create content about social awareness, online safety, education, technology and everyday issues that matter to ordinary people.

My vision is to keep developing myself, support students through accessible learning resources and contribute to the improvement of my locality and community. I believe real progress begins when we keep learning and use what we know to help others.

Articles & reality checks

Practical explainers and reflections on digital safety, education, technology and everyday society.

Digital safety · Reality Check

Stop, Think, Verify: How to recognise online scams

Scammers often create urgency with fake KYC alerts, lottery messages, free gifts and customer-care numbers.

Read article

Never share an OTP, UPI PIN, password or banking code with anyone. A genuine support agent does not need your secret PIN. Do not trust a phone number simply because it appears in a message or search result. Find the official website or app yourself and use its verified support channel.

Do not install unknown screen-sharing or remote-access apps at the request of a caller. If a message threatens immediate account closure or promises an unbelievable reward, pause. Verify independently before clicking, paying or sharing information. If you suspect fraud, contact your bank through its official channel and report it promptly through the appropriate cybercrime reporting service in your country.

Online awareness

Before you shop online: compare more than the price

A low price is useful only when the seller, product details and return conditions are trustworthy.

Read article

Compare the final checkout price, delivery charges, seller ratings, product specifications and return or replacement policy. Read recent reviews carefully and look for repeated patterns rather than relying on one comment. Check whether the product is sold by a reliable seller and whether the warranty is clearly explained.

Keep your order confirmation and payment record. Avoid payment links sent by unknown people. A little research before ordering can prevent disappointment later.

Technology · AI

Using AI wisely: a helper, not a replacement for thinking

AI tools can help explain concepts, organise ideas and support learning—but they can also make mistakes.

Read article

Use AI to brainstorm, practise, simplify difficult topics and check your understanding. Verify important facts using reliable books, teachers or trusted sources. Never assume a confident answer is automatically correct.

Protect personal information. Do not upload passwords, private documents or sensitive details into tools unless you understand how that service handles data. Your judgement, creativity and responsibility remain important.

Education

Learning beyond examinations

Marks matter, but curiosity, communication and consistent understanding matter throughout life.

Read article

Build a habit of asking questions, explaining a topic in your own words and revisiting what you learned. Break a large chapter into smaller sections. Practise regularly instead of depending only on last-minute study.

Use mistakes as feedback. Ask teachers for clarification when a concept is confusing, and connect classroom learning with examples from everyday life. Education is not only about remembering answers; it is also about learning how to think.

Society · Citizenship

Responsible citizenship begins with everyday actions

A stronger community grows when people stay informed, respect one another and take responsibility.

Read article

Check information before forwarding it. Treat people with dignity, follow lawful processes and help others access accurate public information. Disagreement does not need to become hostility.

Small actions—keeping public spaces clean, supporting education, reporting genuine problems through proper channels and listening to different viewpoints—can contribute to a healthier society.

Motivation · Personal growth

Keep learning, even when progress feels slow

Meaningful progress is usually built through small, repeatable steps rather than one dramatic moment.

Read article

Choose one realistic goal, divide it into manageable actions and review your progress. Learn from feedback without letting one setback define your future. Ask for guidance when you need it and make room for rest and balance.

Success can mean different things to different people. Build skills, act with integrity and measure growth by the effort and learning you put in over time.
